incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Private/VPC cluster autoscaler errors detected for customer cluster 'acme-onprem-3' — GPU queue length > 900, autoscaler attempts failing (provision timeouts). Paging oncall(s): @Ava, @Sam.

Ava (oncall-sre): I'm on it. Confirming impact: which models are in flight?

Priya (ml-eng): seeing sustained enqueue for large-gen models (redwood-llm-70B-q4) — latency skyrocketing, many requests throttled with 429s. Non-critical batches timing out.

Sam (infra-ops): looking at node provisioner logs; provision attempts keep failing with `timeout waiting for node to be Ready` and `provider: insufficient capacity` back from the provisioning agent. This is an on-prem cluster (PXE + Ironic) so looks like image provisioning stalls.

Ava (oncall-sre): @Sam paste the failing log lines?

Sam (infra-ops): here —

```
Apr 18 03:21:14 provisioner[pid=4211] ERROR: boot workflow timed out for node id=ipmi-12-34-56
Apr 18 03:21:14 provisioner[pid=4211] WARN: failed to set provisioning state: Insufficient resources: NIC driver timeout
kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving: pod/gpu-launcher-7f6c4   0/1   ContainerCreating  0   5m
```

Priya (ml-eng): that matches the request pattern — large models queued for GPU-only nodes. If provisioning is stuck, the autoscaler will keep queuing and throttle new requests (we're hitting our router-level concurrency guards).

Jordan (customer-success): Customer 'Acme Corp' has multiple live endpoints; business-impacted customers flagged. I've DM'd their infra lead to let them know we're investigating. They reported timeouts ~03:15 UTC.

Luca (oncall-night): handoff note: this will go across the bridge to day oncall if we don't get nodes online in 30m. @Maya will you be available for escalation?

Maya (eng-sre): available. Quick checklist: 1) confirm autoscaler isn't hitting configured max nodes, 2) check taints/tolerations mismatch, 3) check provisioning agent health on baremetal.

Sam (infra-ops): autoscaler status shows repeated scale-up attempts but failing — maxNodes not yet hit (max=40, current=18). However, there are many 'Unprovisionable' counts due to PXE timeouts. Also noticed nodeTemplate has a legacy taint `dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule` which is expected, but some launcher pods expect tolerations; double-checking.

Ava (oncall-sre): if maxNodes not hit, it's a provisioning failure rather than auth/quota. Two immediate mitigations: 1) reduce incoming concurrency for impacted endpoints to limit queue growth, 2) enable fallback model routing to smaller CPU-backed model for non-critical traffic. Can we patch router to lower concurrency quickly?

Priya (ml-eng): we can route non-SLAs to redwood-llm-7B-cpu variant. I'll prepare a temporary rollout.

deploy-bot: deploy request created by Priya to route model alias `acme-gen-primary` -> `redwood-llm-7B-cpu` (canary 10%). Approval required by oncall.

Ava (oncall-sre): approved. Priya, flip the canary and monitor.

Priya (ml-eng): canary at 10% -> 50% -> 100% in progress. Monitoring token consumption and 429s.

Sam (infra-ops): meanwhile I can manually kick the provisioning agent on the headnodes and restart the PXE service; that could unblock ~4 nodes. Doing: `systemctl restart ironic` and `journalctl -u provisioning -f`.

Sam (infra-ops): after restart, 3 nodes returned to Ready within 8 minutes. Autoscaler registered them. Queue depth dropped ~35%.

Ava (oncall-sre): good. But we still have a backlog and some failing requests. What's the long-term cause?

Sam (infra-ops): tentative root cause: on-prem imaging infra had a flaky NIC firmware on a subset of drive bays. When the autoscaler requested new nodes, many requests got stuck at PXE stage. I filed a hardware ticket with Acme's on-prem team — they have to reseat NICs / update firmware.

Maya (eng-sre): note — the autoscaler didn't surface 'Unprovisionable' in dashboard prominently; we'll add an alert rule to catch repeated PXE timeouts and mark nodes as Unprovisionable earlier.

Jordan (customer-success): Acme infra lead acknowledged the firmware bug and scheduled reseating for 11:00 their local time. They're asking for traffic to be routed to Redwood Dedicated for mission-critical endpoints until then.

Ava (oncall-sre): options: 1) temporarily route critical customers to Hosted Dedicated (requires approval + quota), 2) increase canary of CPU fallback for non-critical, 3) disable large-model scheduling to free GPU queue. Which do we prefer?

Priya (ml-eng): increase fallback to 100% for non-critical, and for critical endpoints we can failover to Hosted Dedicated per Jordan's request. I'll coordinate.

Maya (eng-sre): I'll patch the autoscaler dashboard and create an alert: "ProvisionerTimeouts > 3 in 5m" -> pager. Also add runbook pointer to check PXE/IPMI logs.

Ava (oncall-sre): logging actions:
- Patched router concurrency rules (reduced per-endpoint concurrency by 30%)
- Priya rolled fallback to 100% for non-SLA traffic
- Sam restarted provisioning service; +3 nodes recovered
- Jordan coordinating hosted Dedicated failover with sales/ops for critical customers

Sam (infra-ops): after nodes recovered, autoscaler scaled pods onto new nodes and GPU queue decreased to 120 (from 900). Latency improved. Still watching for recurrence.

deploy-bot: canary -> 100% completed for `acme-gen-primary` -> `redwood-llm-7B-cpu`.

Jordan (customer-success): Acme's engineer confirms they saw reduced failures after the firmware reseat started. They're happy with redirect to Hosted Dedicated for the subset we moved.

Luca (oncall-night): handoff to day team: summary for next oncall — provisioning agent instability caused major queue spike; mitigations taken: router concurrency reduced, CPU fallback enabled, provisioning service restarted, hardware ticket opened with customer. Follow-ups: permanent alert, improve autoscaler metadata, consider pre-warming nodes for large-gen workloads.

Maya (eng-sre): assigning follow-ups: 
- (Maya) Add ProvisionerTimeout alert + dashboard widget (ETA EOD)
- (Sam) Work with infra team to add retry/backoff improvements in provisioner (ETA 2w)
- (Priya) Build model routing playbook for emergency CPU fallback (ETA 1w)
- (Jordan) Confirm hosted Dedicated billing/contract approval flow for emergency failovers (ETA today)

Ava (oncall-sre): creating incident ticket and postmortem stub. Severity: Sev 2 (customer-impacting, mitigated). Will include timeline and RFO.

Priya (ml-eng): one note — we should add a runbook step to lower `max_model_size` for private clusters when Unprovisionable > X to avoid repeated autoscaler churn. I'll draft it.

Ava (oncall-sre): thanks all. Closing real-time updates. If anything spikes again, re-ping this thread. :white_check_mark:
